changes.summary: First published data: 986 towns, 79 with a documented name history, with name stories and pronunciation guides.
Renamed airports, dams and a mountain pass are now on the map, e.g. Jan Smuts → O. R. Tambo International Airport and Hendrik Verwoerd Dam → Gariep Dam.
Clearer wording in three town notes (Louis Trichardt, Vaalwater and Reitz).

Eight more renamed towns (e.g. Brandfort → Winnie Mandela, Mount Fletcher → Tlokoeng, Melmoth → eMthonjaneni), rename years corrected to the official gazette dates, the spelling Bela-Bela, and the full Louis Trichardt story.

towns.name: Bhisho
towns.notes: Former capital of the Ciskei homeland.

towns.name: Cape Town International Airport
towns.notes: Opened in 1954 as Bellville Airport and soon named after prime minister D. F. Malan; renamed Cape Town International in the early 1990s.

towns.name: Centurion
towns.notes: Originally Lyttelton; renamed Verwoerdburg in 1967, then Centurion in 1994.

towns.name: Chief Dawid Stuurman International Airport
towns.notes: Later known as Port Elizabeth (International) Airport; renamed Chief Dawid Stuurman International Airport in February 2021.

towns.name: Ekhephini
towns.notes: Gazetted 6 Feb 2026. Under review after more than 38,000 objections (as of May 2026), so the old name is still widely used.

towns.name: Gariep Dam
towns.notes: Renamed on 4 October 1996. South Africa's largest reservoir, on the Orange River.

towns.name: King Phalo Airport
towns.notes: Called East London Airport from 1994; renamed King Phalo Airport in February 2021.

towns.name: KuGompo City
towns.notes: Gazetted 6 Feb 2026. Under review after more than 38,000 objections (as of May 2026), so the old name is still widely used.

towns.name: KwaDukuza
towns.notes: Historic capital of the Zulu kingdom under Shaka.

towns.name: Louis Trichardt
towns.notes: Renamed Makhado in 2003; the Supreme Court of Appeal set this aside in 2007. It was renamed Makhado again in 2011, and the High Court set that aside in 2014, so its official name is Louis Trichardt.

towns.name: Mahikeng
towns.notes: Originally Mafeking; spelled Mafikeng from 1980, renamed Mahikeng in 2010.

towns.name: Makhanda
towns.notes: Renamed after the Xhosa warrior-prophet Makhanda (Nxele).

towns.name: Mbombela
towns.notes: Provincial capital of Mpumalanga.

towns.name: Mbombo Pass
towns.notes: Gazetted 6 Feb 2026 with the other Eastern Cape renames, which are under review after more than 38,000 objections (as of May 2026).

towns.name: Mthatha
towns.notes: Former capital of the Transkei homeland.

towns.name: O. R. Tambo International Airport
towns.notes: Called Johannesburg International Airport from 1994 until 2006.

towns.name: Polokwane
towns.notes: Provincial capital of Limpopo.

towns.name: Reitz
towns.notes: Founded as Singer's Post, then called Amsterdam, and renamed Reitz in the late 1880s after Free State president F. W. Reitz - so it has been Reitz for well over a century.

towns.name: Robert Sobukwe Town
towns.notes: Gazetted 6 Feb 2026. Under review after more than 38,000 objections (as of May 2026), so the old name is still widely used.

towns.name: Vaalwater
towns.notes: Renamed Mabatlane in 2006 and reverted to Vaalwater in 2007, so its previous name is the same as today's.

towns.name: Vanderkloof Dam
towns.notes: On the Orange River, between the Northern Cape and the Free State.

towns.name: Xamdeboo
towns.notes: Gazetted 6 Feb 2026. Under review after more than 38,000 objections (as of May 2026), so the old name is still widely used.

towns.name: Bishop Limba
towns.notes: Gazetted 6 Feb 2026 with the other Eastern Cape renames, which are under review after more than 38,000 objections (as of May 2026).

stories.name: Bela-Bela
stories.meaning: Setswana for ‘the pot that boils’ – after the hot springs the town was built around.
stories.formerNameOrigin: Warmbad (Warmbaths in English) meant the same thing: ‘warm bath’.

stories.name: Bhisho
stories.meaning: Usually explained as the isiXhosa word for buffalo, which is also the name of the river here. The new spelling is the standard isiXhosa one.

stories.name: Cacadu
stories.meaning: ‘Bulrush water’ – the isiXhosa name for the White Kei River, which rises in the district.
stories.formerNameOrigin: Lady Frere was named after the wife of Sir Henry Bartle Frere, Cape governor from 1877 to 1880.

stories.name: Cape Town International Airport
stories.formerNameOrigin: Named after D. F. Malan, prime minister when the airport opened in 1954.

stories.name: Centane
stories.meaning: Same name, now written in standard isiXhosa spelling.

stories.name: Centurion
stories.formerNameOrigin: Verwoerdburg (1967) was named after prime minister Hendrik Verwoerd, regarded as the architect of apartheid.

stories.name: Dikeni
stories.formerNameOrigin: Alice was named in 1847 after Princess Alice, Queen Victoria's second daughter.

stories.name: Dutywa
stories.meaning: Same name, now written in standard isiXhosa spelling.

stories.name: eMakhazeni
stories.formerNameOrigin: Belfast was named after the Northern Irish birthplace of Richard Charles O'Neil, who owned the farm.

stories.name: Emalahleni
stories.meaning: ‘Place of coal’.
stories.formerNameOrigin: Witbank is Afrikaans for ‘white ridge’, after a white sandstone outcrop.

stories.name: eManzana
stories.meaning: ‘Healing waters’ – the name Swazi people gave the hot spring here.
stories.formerNameOrigin: Badplaas is Afrikaans for ‘bath farm’.

stories.name: eManzimtoti
stories.meaning: ‘Sweet water’ – said to be King Shaka's words on tasting the river. He used ‘mtoti’ instead of the usual ‘mnandi’ out of respect for his mother, Nandi.

stories.name: eMaxesibeni
stories.formerNameOrigin: Mount Ayliff was possibly named after William Ayliff, a Cape official, or John Ayliff, a mission founder.

stories.name: eMdloti
stories.meaning: Same name, now written in standard isiZulu spelling; the e- at the start means ‘at’ or ‘the place of’.

stories.name: Emgwenya
stories.formerNameOrigin: Waterval Boven is Dutch for ‘above the waterfall’.

stories.name: eMkhomazi
stories.meaning: ‘Place of the cow whales’ – whales were seen in the river mouth.

stories.name: eMkhondo
stories.formerNameOrigin: Piet Retief was named after the Voortrekker leader Piet Retief.

stories.name: eMkhuze
stories.meaning: Same name, now written in standard isiZulu spelling; the e- at the start means ‘at’ or ‘the place of’.

stories.name: eMthunzini
stories.meaning: ‘A place in the shade’ in isiZulu.

stories.name: eNtokozweni
stories.meaning: ‘Place of happiness’.
stories.formerNameOrigin: Machadodorp honoured Portuguese Major Joachim Machado (1894).

stories.name: eXobho
stories.meaning: An isiZulu word imitating the squelch of cattle walking through mud.

stories.name: Gariep Dam
stories.meaning: Gariep is Khoekhoe for ‘river’ – the original name of the Orange River, which the dam holds back.
stories.formerNameOrigin: Originally named after prime minister Hendrik Verwoerd.

stories.name: Gcuwa
stories.formerNameOrigin: Butterworth was named after Joseph Butterworth.

stories.name: Gqeberha
stories.meaning: The isiXhosa and Southern Khoe name for the Baakens River, which runs through the city. It is also the isiXhosa name for Walmer Township, one of the city's oldest townships.
stories.formerNameOrigin: Port Elizabeth was named in 1820 by acting governor Sir Rufane Donkin after his late wife, Elizabeth.

stories.name: James Calata
stories.meaning: Honours Canon James Arthur Calata (1895–1983), Anglican priest in nearby Cradock for forty years and ANC secretary-general from 1936 to 1949.
stories.formerNameOrigin: Jamestown was named after James Wagenaar, who owned the farm the town was laid out on.

stories.name: Kariega
stories.meaning: The area's original inhabitants called the Swartkops River the Kariega River, and the wider region from Willowmore and Somerset East to Uitenhage was once called Kariega.

stories.name: Khowa
stories.formerNameOrigin: Elliot was named after Sir Henry George Elliot, chief magistrate of the Transkeian territories from 1891 to 1902.

stories.name: King Phalo Airport
stories.formerNameOrigin: Named after Ben Schoeman, the minister of transport at the time.

stories.name: Komani
stories.formerNameOrigin: Queenstown was named after Queen Victoria.

stories.name: KuGompo City
stories.meaning: From Gompo Rock (Cove Rock) on the coast, a sacred place for amaXhosa. The name is said to echo the waves breaking on it – ‘gompo, gompo’. ‘City’ was added because a small town already had the name KuGompo.

stories.name: KwaBhaca
stories.meaning: ‘Place of the Bhaca people’ – the village of the amaBhaca chiefdom.
stories.formerNameOrigin: Mount Frere was named after Sir Henry Bartle Frere.

stories.name: KwaDukuza
stories.meaning: ‘Place of the lost person’ in isiZulu – after the maze of huts at King Shaka's royal capital here.
stories.formerNameOrigin: Stanger (1873) was named after William Stanger, surveyor-general of Natal.

stories.name: KwaGingindlovu
stories.meaning: ‘Swallower of the elephant’ – one of Cetshwayo's military homesteads, named for his 1856 victory over his brother Mbuyazi.

stories.name: KwaMaqoma
stories.meaning: Honours Maqoma, the Xhosa warrior chief who resisted British colonial forces in this area.
stories.formerNameOrigin: Fort Beaufort was named after the Duke of Beaufort.

stories.name: KwaNojoli
stories.meaning: Honours Nojoli, a royal figure in the history of the amaXhosa of this area.

stories.name: Lephalale
stories.meaning: Named after the main river here; from a Setswana word meaning ‘to flow’.
stories.formerNameOrigin: Ellisras combined the surnames of settlers Patrick Ellis and Piet Erasmus.

stories.name: Mahikeng
stories.meaning: ‘Place among rocks’ in Setswana. British settlers wrote it as Mafeking.

stories.name: Makhanda
stories.meaning: Honours Makhanda ka Nxele, the Xhosa warrior and prophet who led the 1819 attack on the British garrison here and was later imprisoned on Robben Island.
stories.formerNameOrigin: Grahamstown was named after Colonel John Graham, who oversaw its founding in 1812.

stories.name: Malalane
stories.meaning: Same name, with a corrected spelling.

stories.name: Maletswai
stories.formerNameOrigin: Aliwal North was named by Sir Harry Smith after his victory over the Sikhs at the Battle of Aliwal.

stories.name: Maloti
stories.meaning: Same name, now written with the Sesotho spelling (Maloti rather than Maluti).

stories.name: Mashishing
stories.meaning: ‘Long green grass’ in Sepedi – what the Bapedi called the area.
stories.formerNameOrigin: Lydenburg comes from the Dutch Lijdenburg, ‘town of suffering’.

stories.name: Mbizana
stories.meaning: Same name, now written in standard isiXhosa spelling.

stories.name: Mbombela
stories.meaning: ‘Many people together in a small space’ in siSwati.
stories.formerNameOrigin: Nelspruit was named after the Nel family who grazed cattle here, with spruit, an Afrikaans word for a stream.

stories.name: Modimolle
stories.meaning: From the Sotho-Tswana Modimo o lle, ‘the spirit has eaten’ or ‘God has eaten’ – the local name of a hill here.
stories.formerNameOrigin: Nylstroom: the Voortrekkers thought the river was the Nile (Nyl) and the hill a pyramid.

stories.name: Modjadjiskloof
stories.meaning: Honours Rain Queen Modjadji, hereditary ruler of the Lobedu people. It keeps the Afrikaans -kloof (ravine).
stories.formerNameOrigin: Duiwelskloof is Afrikaans for ‘Devil's ravine’.

stories.name: Mokopane
stories.meaning: Honours King (Chief) Mokopane, also written Makapan, of the Kekana Ndebele.
stories.formerNameOrigin: Potgietersrus remembered Voortrekker leader Piet Potgieter, killed in 1854 during the Siege of Makapansgat.

stories.name: Mookgophong
stories.formerNameOrigin: Naboomspruit means ‘euphorbia tree stream’, after the Euphorbia ingens (naboom) trees.

stories.name: Mthatha
stories.meaning: Named after the Mthatha River, which takes its name from the sneezewood (umthathi) trees along it, known for their wood and medicinal uses.

stories.name: Musina
stories.meaning: TshiVenda for copper, from a root meaning ‘spoil’ – copper ‘spoilt’ early efforts to mine gold here.

stories.name: Ngcobo
stories.meaning: Same name, now written in standard isiXhosa spelling.

stories.name: Ngqamakhwe
stories.meaning: Same name, now written in standard isiXhosa spelling.

stories.name: Ngqeleni
stories.meaning: Same name, now written in standard isiXhosa spelling.

stories.name: Nqanqarhu
stories.meaning: The town began in 1876 as a military camp called Nqanqaru Drift.
stories.formerNameOrigin: Maclear was named after astronomer Sir Thomas Maclear.

stories.name: Ntabankulu
stories.meaning: Same name, now written in standard isiXhosa spelling.

stories.name: Ntabozuko
stories.formerNameOrigin: Berlin was founded in 1857 by German settlers and named after the German capital.

stories.name: Nxuba
stories.formerNameOrigin: Cradock was named after Sir John Cradock, governor of the Cape Colony in the early 1800s.

stories.name: O. R. Tambo International Airport
stories.meaning: Honours Oliver Reginald Tambo (1917–1993), anti-apartheid leader and president of the ANC from 1967 to 1991.
stories.formerNameOrigin: Opened in 1952 as Jan Smuts International Airport, after the former prime minister.

stories.name: oThongathi
stories.meaning: From the uThongathi River. In isiZulu it means ‘it is important to us’ or ‘you are important because of us’, linked to legends about King Shaka.

stories.name: Polokwane
stories.meaning: ‘Sanctuary’ in Sepedi (Northern Sotho) – a name Sepedi speakers already used for the area.
stories.formerNameOrigin: Pietersburg (1886) honoured Voortrekker leader Petrus Jacobus (Piet) Joubert.

stories.name: Qonce
stories.meaning: The Khoikhoi name for the Buffalo River, on which the town stands.
stories.formerNameOrigin: King William's Town was named after King William IV.

stories.name: Robert Sobukwe Town
stories.meaning: Honours Robert Mangaliso Sobukwe, who was born here, anti-apartheid leader and founding president of the Pan Africanist Congress (PAC).
stories.formerNameOrigin: Graaff-Reinet was named after Cape governor Cornelis Jacob van de Graaff and his wife.

stories.name: uMnambithi
stories.formerNameOrigin: Ladysmith (1850) was named after Juana María de los Dolores de León Smith, wife of governor Sir Harry Smith.

stories.name: Mamafubedu
stories.formerNameOrigin: The town was to be called Concordia, but Petrus Paulus Steyn's widow sold the land on condition that it was named after her late husband.

stories.name: Hlohlolwane
stories.meaning: From Sesotho words meaning 'get up and fight', after a dispute between the Bakwena and Baphuthi over a maize harvest.
stories.formerNameOrigin: Clocolan is how newer residents said 'Hlohlolwane'.

stories.name: Winnie Mandela
stories.meaning: Honours Winnie Madikizela-Mandela, who was banished to the town in 1977. Her house there is now a museum.
stories.formerNameOrigin: Brandfort was named after Johannes Brand, President of the Orange Free State, who visited soon after the town was founded in 1874.

stories.name: Tlokoeng
stories.meaning: Sesotho for 'place of the Tlokoa clan'.
stories.formerNameOrigin: Mount Fletcher was named after the nearby mountain, probably after Reverend John Fletcher, a friend of John Wesley.

stories.name: Gxarha
stories.formerNameOrigin: Morgan's Bay was named in 1822 after A. F. Morgan, master of the survey ship Barracouta.

stories.name: Solomon Linda
stories.meaning: Honours Solomon Linda, the musician born here, a pioneer of isicathamiya choral music.
stories.formerNameOrigin: Pomeroy was named after Sir George Pomeroy Colley, the British commander at the Battle of Majuba Hill in 1881.

stories.name: Bishop Limba
stories.formerNameOrigin: Adendorp was named after N. J. Adendorff, who owned the farm and divided it into smallholdings around 1858.

stories.name: eMthonjaneni
stories.formerNameOrigin: Melmoth was named after Sir Melmoth Osborn, the British resident commissioner of Zululand.
